thread:
maria: Heads up — saw EU-west GPU pools back up around 10:12 UTC. Queue depth spiked and admission didn't throttle quickly. Investigating token accounting mismatch.
kevin: yikes. any obvious evictions or preemptibles?
maria: yes, we had 3 preemptible node evictions in the last 5m for pool-eu-gpu-a; pods got rescheduled but token ledger still showed old capacity for ~40s.
ali: that would let requests get admitted > effective TPM for short window. did queue length increase?
maria: queued_count P90 went from 12 -> 260 in ~60s, queued_age P95 hit 4.1s. latency + token_drain_rate graphs attached (link).
jamie: can you paste the refill/logs? curious how our refill EWMA handled the sudden capacity drop.
maria: pasted metric dump: ```
# /metrics snapshot
redwood_tokens_available{pool=\"eu-gpu-a\"} 1200
redwood_tpm_limit{pool=\"eu-gpu-a\"} 300
token_refill_rate{pool=\"eu-gpu-a\"} 5.0
token_ledger_headroom{pool=\"eu-gpu-a\"} 0.04
queued_count{pool=\"eu-gpu-a\"} 260
queued_age_p95{pool=\"eu-gpu-a\"} 4.12
```\nkevin: token_ledger_headroom 0.04 (4%) is dangerously low; with preemptible evictions ledger didn't reconcile until node controller tear-down finished.
ali: The root is that admission uses the last-known capacity + a smear buffer. When nodes disappear fast, smear stays positive and admits until we detect loss. Need faster reconciliation or a different circuit.
jamie: Agree. Two tolerances: (1) rapid capacity-change detection, (2) a short-term circuit-breaker that clamps admission if queued growth slope > threshold.
maria: proposal: add an \"admission-degradation\" state machine: if queued_count derivative > X and queued_age_p95 > Y, immediately reduce admission target to min(ledger, conservative_tpm) and start reconciling nodes. This buys time for KV cache to flush.
kevin: what values for X/Y? from this incident queued derivative ~ +200/60s => ~3.3 req/s. queued_age_p95 4.1s. perhaps X=2 req/s and Y=2s?
ali: also tie to token_drain_rate. If token_drain_rate > refill_rate * 1.5 for >10s, flip circuit. That captures token runaway even without evictions.
jamie: we should avoid false positives for canary traffic. Canaries are low qps but high latency. maybe add an override window for routes marked canary.
kevin: good call. add route-level metadata: allow_circuit_override=true|false. default false.
maria: added a short runbook suggestion: 1) when circuit flips, route new requests to fallback model-variant or regional fallback for 60s; 2) emit metric admission_circuit_state{pool,reason}; 3) force immediate token ledger reconciliation.
ali: will simulate in the admission-sim harness. I already have a branch that can toggle the derivative threshold. Running quick sim: baseline token-ledgers with smear=10s then 3-node eviction at t=120s.
(ops-bot): deploy pipeline triggered: canary/admission-circuit-sim -> test-cluster (job/4532).
kevin: results?
ali: initial run: without circuit, admitted spike = +320 requests, queued_age_p95 4.8s, tail latency 620ms; with circuit enabled (X=2,Y=2,drain_ratio=1.5) admitted spike capped at +40, queued_age_p95 1.9s. CPU for controller increased +7% due to extra reconciliation calls.
maria: that looks promising. what about costs? more reconciliation = more API calls but saves huge tail costs and customer latency.
jamie: agree. one more edge: KV cache stale keys. if KV cache still pointing at pods that died we might overcount available token slots. Add a TTL on cache entries shorter when backlog > threshold.
kevin: TTL reduce from 30s -> 5s under high backlog sounds reasonable. Also emit metric kv_cache_stale_evictions.
ali: items for PR: (1) admission circuit state machine + metrics, (2) derivative and drain-ratio thresholds + config, (3) route-level override metadata, (4) adaptive kv cache TTL under backpressure, (5) e2e sim job and canary.
maria: I'll own the runbook update and postmortem blurb. Kevin will own the config and metrics. Ali will own sim and PR. Jamie handles canary gating/overrides.
kevin: timeline? can we get a canary in 48h?
ali: I can get a sim + unit tests in 24h, PR next day, then canary in 48-72h depending on reviews.
maria: Ops: when we roll, watch metrics: admission_circuit_state, token_drain_rate, queued_count, queued_age_p95. Alert if circuit flips > 3 times in 1h.
jamie: also add a dashboard tile for regional fallback traffic and fallback_success_rate.
(ops-bot): ticket created: INFRA-8423 admission-circuit and kv-ttl under backpressure (assignee: ali).
kevin: thanks — nice mitigation path.
maria: thanks team. I'll post a short notes thread in #incidents if anything else shows up.
